properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 12 at 7:21AM EDT until September 12 at 1:15PM EDT by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
FFWFFC

The National Weather Service in Peachtree City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Cobb County in north central Georgia...
Northwestern Douglas County in north central Georgia...
Central Carroll County in northwestern Georgia...
Southeastern Paulding County in northwestern Georgia...

* Until 115 PM EDT.

* At 721 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Douglasville, Carrollton, Dallas, Villa Rica, Powder Springs,
Austell, Temple, Hiram, Mount Zion, Lithia Springs, Lake
Val-Do-Mar, Winston, New Georgia, Bill Arp, Treasure Lake,
Brownsville, Abilene, Lost Mountain Park and Due West.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 12 at 11:52AM EDT until September 12 at 1:45PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee
River Fl out to 20 Nm...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...
Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 145 PM EDT.

* At 1151 AM EDT, a cluster of strong thunderstorms capable of
producing waterspouts were located along a line extending from 8
nm north of O Tower to near Suwannee River, moving east at 25
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Buckeye Reef, Horseshoe Beach, K Tower, Marker 24 Barge, and
Suwannee River.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.
